title: Agimat and the World Beyond
cultural_note: An agimat is an amulet or talisman in Filipino folk belief, said to protect or empower the person who carries it.

screenshots.alt: Two small heroes face a row of giant shadow creatures with glowing red eyes
A blue dragon rises out of the darkness

short_description: A 2D platformer adventure built on creatures from Philippine mythology.
description: Agimat and the World Beyond is a 2D platformer based on Philippine mythology from Laguna-based Boom Brain Studio. Its devlog introduces two heroes, Lukas and Lily, who travel to a world called Atycia. The game was launched on Kickstarter in August 2020 as a pandemic project.

title: Agnostiko ORIGINS
cultural_note: The aswang and the kapre are two of the best-known creatures of Philippine folklore: a shape-shifter that preys at night, and a tall tree giant said to smoke a cigar.

screenshots.alt: The hero rides a platform inside a clock tower full of gears
The hero fights a winged, horse-bodied creature in a hall with red curtains
Map of Mr. Plague's Mansion
The hero battles a hulking creature under a crescent moon

short_description: A 16-bit style Metroidvania set in a steampunk 1890s Manila full of mythological monsters.
description: Agnostiko ORIGINS is a 2D Metroidvania by solo developer Leoned Andrew Tumbaga under the Singles Alliance name. It is set in a steampunk Philippines of the 1890s, where monsters drawn from Philippine mythology roam Manila. It was released for Nintendo Switch on June 14, 2024.
highlights: Metroidvania exploration in 16-bit style pixel art
Monsters from Philippine mythology, such as the aswang and kapre

title: Anito: Defend a Land Enraged
cultural_note: Anito are the ancestor and nature spirits of pre-colonial Philippine belief. The word was also used for carved figures that represented them.

screenshots.alt: Title art: three characters above the words Anito, Defend a Land Enraged
Isometric view of a furnished room with a staircase and a woven rug
Isometric view of a busy village market
A burning field seen from above

short_description: A 2003 role-playing game based on Filipino mythology and folklore.
description: Anito: Defend a Land Enraged is a role-playing game for Windows by Manila studio Anino Entertainment, released in 2003. It is often described as the first video game produced and designed entirely by a team of Filipino developers. It won the Innovation in Audio award at the 2004 Independent Games Festival.
highlights: Role-playing game based on Filipino mythology and folklore
Innovation in Audio award, Independent Games Festival 2004

title: Aswang Hunter
cultural_note: The aswang is a shape-shifter in Philippine folklore, often said to pass as an ordinary neighbour by day. Salt and garlic are among the traditional protections.

screenshots.alt: First-person view: the player raises a bolo as a winged Wakwak attacks
A dark room with the choices Talk, Give weapon and Hide above a sleeping man
First-person view: the player swings a hammer at a creature labelled Sigbin
A pregnant woman sits bleeding on a toilet in a dim bathroom

short_description: A real-time horror battler about protecting families from an aswang outbreak until dawn.
description: Aswang Hunter mixes real-time horror combat with house defence. As a rogue hunter you explore vulnerable homes, watch the silhouettes in the windows, and protect families from an aswang outbreak, scavenging bolos and spears and controlling each arm separately. It is coming to Steam; the release date has not been announced.
highlights: Real-time battles combined with house defence
Scavenge bolos and spears, and control each arm

title: Bayani
cultural_note: Bayani means hero. Some of the game's fighters are inspired by figures from Philippine history, such as Apolinario Mabini.

screenshots.alt: Joe fights Fernando on a stage with a monument and city towers
Rio fights Oria in a burst of hit sparks
Dre fights Leon on a ruined city stage
Tonio, a bandaged brawler, squares up to Oria
Joe lands a seven-hit combo on Dre

short_description: A 1-on-1 fighting game inspired by Philippine history, culture and mythology.
description: BAYANI is a 1-on-1 indie fighting game by Ranida Games, heavily inspired by the Philippines' history, culture and mythology. It combines 2D fighting with full 3D graphics, and uses simplified six-button controls for fast-paced play. Its Steam page calls it the first commercial fighting game developed in the Philippines.

title: Breadwinner
cultural_note: In many Filipino families one member, the breadwinner, supports parents and siblings from a single salary.

screenshots.alt: A hooded young man looks at his phone on a dark street between parked vehicles
A phone screen listing planned payments for the month: food, Nanay's medicine and fare
The young man walks past a wall covered in posters at night
Tatay on the sofa says: No money for me again, huh?
A child draws at a table lit by a candle
A social media feed on the phone, with a cash-advance ad

short_description: Split one salary across your family. The money is never enough for it all.
description: Breadwinner is a game about supporting a family on one salary. On a phone screen you plan the month's payments, such as food for the house, Nanay's medicine and the fare to work, and deal with what the family asks of you. The studio and the official page are still to be confirmed.

title: Eskinita
cultural_note: An eskinita is a narrow alley between houses. A lugawan is a small stall that sells lugaw, a rice porridge often eaten late at night.

screenshots.alt: Three customers wait at the lugaw stall counter at night
The Gola-Gola lugawan stall at the end of a dark alley
A customer eats lugaw at the counter
A parked van on a dim street lit by one lamp
A small bedroom with a striped bed and an electric fan
A dark alley with graffiti on the walls

short_description: Close up a neighbourhood lugawan late at night, then survive the walk home.
description: ESKINITA is a short, atmospheric Filipino-inspired suspense horror game about working late nights in a small neighbourhood lugawan and surviving the walk home through dark alleys. At first it is only little things, until one night they start following you.

title: Hapunan
cultural_note: Hapunan means dinner. Balut, a boiled fertilised duck egg, is a street food often sold at night by vendors calling out in the neighbourhood.

screenshots.alt: Passengers ride inside a jeepney through the countryside
A man in a suit sits behind trays of eggs lit by a lamp
Inventory screen showing a balut, a fertilised duck egg

short_description: A teenager and his father turn to late-night street vending, and dark secrets uncoil behind the trade.
description: Hapunan is a story-driven psychological horror game steeped in Filipino urban legends. Facing eviction, a teenager and his father turn to late-night street vending to survive, selling balut. As dark secrets uncoil behind the trade, every choice decides who eats and who survives. It was first released on itch.io for Windows and Android.

title: Jeepney Simulator
cultural_note: Jeepneys, first built from leftover US military jeeps, are one of the best-known forms of public transport in the Philippines. Their bright paint and slogans make each one different.

screenshots.alt: First-person view from the driver's seat at a city intersection at dusk
A jeepney parked at a gas station
Top-down view of traffic with fuel trucks and a jeepney
Inside a jeepney full of passengers, heading to Breeze Mall
A jeepney passes a lit-up HIRAYA sign at night

short_description: Pick up passengers, calculate change, and weave through traffic in a Filipino-made driving game.
description: Jeepney Simulator puts you behind the wheel of a jeepney. Pick up passengers, calculate their change, and weave through traffic. Feed your family, customise your jeepneys, and unlock more rides. It mixes a casual driving sim with resource management, and left Early Access on Steam in September 2023.
highlights: Pick up passengers and make change

title: Kalayaan Road: The Story of Kuya Jesse
cultural_note: Kalayaan means freedom. Pares, braised beef served with garlic rice and broth, is a staple of roadside stalls.

screenshots.alt: A food stall shelf with baskets of onions and garlic and a cut of raw beef
A police officer at a desk with Evidence and Cases binders
A city street with a 'Pabahay ni Makisig' billboard and road barriers
A hospital waiting area with children and a grandmother on the benches
Kuya Jesse at his pares cart at night

short_description: The story of Kuya Jesse, a pares vendor, told in chapters.
description: Kalayaan Road: The Story of Kuya Jesse follows Kuya Jesse through chapters of city life: cooking and selling pares from his cart, filing a report at a police station, and waiting at a hospital. The studio and the official page are still to be confirmed.

title: Karinderya ni Mark
cultural_note: A karinderya is a small eatery that serves home-style ulam (viands) from pots on display.

screenshots.alt: Five customers wait by the beach above trays of Filipino dishes
Title menu with Play, Exit and Select buttons
Customers order at the counter of viands

short_description: Run a Filipino eatery and serve every customer the right dish, fast.
description: Karinderya ni Mark is a fast-paced pixel-art cooking game about running a Filipino eatery. Serve customers quickly: wrong dishes or drinks lower the shop's rating, and a rating of zero closes the karinderya. It is available in English and Tagalog.

title: Lola Maria
cultural_note: Lola means grandmother. Many Filipino households are multigenerational, with grandparents living with their children and grandchildren.

screenshots.alt: A handwritten note read by flashlight
A dark living room with old furniture
A kitchen counter with a gas stove in a wooden house
Lola Maria in a checked dress stands in a dim wooden room
A blue tabo, a water dipper, on a bathroom floor

short_description: Live with your grandmother, and watch everyday chores take a disturbing turn.
description: Lola Maria is a first-person psychological horror game where everyday tasks take a disturbing turn. Living with your grandmother, you water the plants, look for missing notes and talk with Lola, and uncover unsettling secrets as the line between family, memory and the supernatural begins to blur.
highlights: Inspired by Filipino traditions and fears

title: Mahika

screenshots.alt: A pixel-art girl walks a stone path in a blue forest
The girl stands on a dirt road between pine trees, with an item bar below
The girl casts a glowing spell in the forest
Top-down view of a café with cats, bookshelves and bean bags
A pixel-art bakery kitchen with cakes on display

short_description: A pixel-art, top-down RPG magic adventure with roguelike elements.
description: Mahika is an action-packed, top-down RPG magic adventure in pixel art, with roguelike elements and a sprinkle of mystery. Its world draws on Filipino and other world cultures and mythologies. It is coming soon to Steam.
highlights: Customisable avatar and a farming system

title: Maiba Taya
cultural_note: 'Maiba taya' is the chant used to pick who will be 'it' (the taya) before a street game such as tag or hide-and-seek.

screenshots.alt: First-person view of kids playing around a big tree
Kids sit on a ledge watching the sunset over the jungle
Hider mode: kids run through the plants while the taya searches
A small sari-sari store in the village
Wooden houses with laundry hanging out to dry
Survivor mode at night: a monster closes in during wave 8

short_description: Co-op survival PvP inspired by classic neighbourhood street games.
description: MAIBA TAYA is a co-op survival PvP game for 3 to 8 players, inspired by classic neighbourhood street games. Run outside until nightfall, compete across chaotic game modes, earn rewards and customise your kid. It is in Early Access on Steam, published by Neuroticfly Games.
highlights: Game modes based on street games

title: Mandato
cultural_note: Mandato means mandate: the authority voters give an elected official.

screenshots.alt: First-person view in an alley, holding a phone with a chat open
A woman eats breakfast at a table under a Last Supper painting
Washing a plate in the sink
Sitting down to a breakfast of rice, egg and hotdog
Taking a photo with the phone in a small room

short_description: A short first-person horror story about a beloved mayor and the town's crimes.
description: MANDATO is a short, first-person horror narrative set in the Philippines. While your journalist wife investigates town hall, you start uncovering brutal secrets that tie your beloved mayor to local crime. Published by Solitary Studios; coming soon to Steam.

title: Patintero
cultural_note: Patintero is a street game where the taya guard lines drawn on the ground while the other team tries to cross without being tagged.

screenshots.alt: A store window with canned sardines and an egg on the counter
A balut vendor's box lit by a candle
Picking up a brick game handheld from a crate
A flashlight finds a Rambo heavy duty slipper in the grass
A candle at a small roadside shrine
A figure stands in thick fog

short_description: Atmospheric first-person horror with Batang 90s childhood nostalgia.
description: Patintero is an atmospheric first-person horror game that blends in 'Batang 90s' childhood nostalgia, named after the traditional Filipino street game. It is available for Windows on itch.io.

title: Sabado

screenshots.alt: A student stands by a basketball court at sunset
Chesa smiles in a hallway lit red
Chesa stands in a classroom
An empty classroom with evening light on the desks
A long hallway that ends in red light
A school library with bookshelves

short_description: Reunite with a cheerful classmate in a shifting maze of high school memories.
description: Sabado is a horror game about reuniting with your favourite classmate. Wander through a nostalgic, shifting maze of old high school memories with a cheerful friend named Chesa, while the exits vanish, the hallways warp, and a silent observer tracks your every step. Published on Steam by Neuroticfly Games.
highlights: A school that changes as you play

title: Taguan
cultural_note: Taguan is the Filipino name for hide-and-seek, from tago, 'to hide'.

screenshots.alt: Construction workers by a 'This is where your taxes go' flood-control sign
Neighbours chat by a wall on a sunny street
An office with cubicles
A man sits slumped against an alley wall marked 'Bawal umihi dito'
A room with a broom, a bench and a table
A dark hallway with a fridge and an electric fan

short_description: A mysterious figure is making people disappear, and the footsteps are getting closer.
description: Taguan is a slow-burn Filipino societal horror game. David Lagani is an ordinary Filipino worker whose quiet life turns to dread when a mysterious figure starts breaking into homes and making people disappear. Each night feels longer and every sound closer. It takes about an hour to finish.

title: Water Delivery
cultural_note: In many Philippine towns, drinking water is delivered to homes in refillable five-gallon jugs.

screenshots.alt: A five-gallon water jug on a table, ready to pick up
The delivery truck on a road at dusk
A small store at night

short_description: Ride the delivery truck on your last route of the evening. Deliver the jugs. Collect the payments.
description: Water Delivery is a first-person horror game where you play a water delivery worker on the final route of the evening. Ride along in the delivery truck from house to house, deliver filled jugs, find and return the empty ones, and collect every payment.
highlights: Multiple endings, based on your choices and what you discover
